question.text: Each scheme of an Alternative Investment Fund must have a minimum corpus of:

explanation.text: The Logic: NISM-Series-X-A (p.235) states that each AIF scheme shall have a corpus of at least Rs. 20 crore, with funds raised through private placement subject to the 1,000-investor cap per scheme. The Trap: Rs. 20 crore is the per-scheme minimum, not a per-fund threshold — an AIF can run multiple schemes, each meeting the corpus floor independently. Note: Rationales about scale economics, concentration risk, or per-unit costs are not in the checked page and should be cited from a separate source before being asserted.
